title: Ballon d’Or 2026 Winners: Full List
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom12:27 PM EDTHarry Kane (left) and Alexia Putellas were the night’s big winners. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty Images• PLEASE CLICK/TAP HERE TO REFRESH FOR LIVE UPDATES TO THIS ARTICLEAs Kylian Mbappé once gushed, capturing the modern obsession with this individual award, the Ballon d’Or is “the Holy Grail,” the “ticket to the big world.”

Real Madrid’s prolific striker was front and center on a night which saw not one, not two, but 13 different prizes dished out at The London Palladium. Yet, Mbappé didn’t receive a single gong. The standout men and women, youngsters, goalkeepers, coaches and clubs were all ruthlessly ranked and categorized by a panel of journalists which collectively overlooked the biggest advocate of the award anywhere.

“We all watched that ceremony with those red carpet arrivals and said to ourselves: One day, that will be me,” Mbappé has admitted. He joined the rest of the great and the good of the sport on that red carpet only to watch on as those golden tickets were handed out elsewhere.

It’s been a long-time coming for Harry Kane. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesAfter spending most of his acceptance speech teetering on the brink of tears, Harry Kane could afford to let out a triumphant cackle once the whole ordeal was over. Less than 15 months ago, Kane had never won a single team trophy in his senior career. Now he stands alone as the greatest player on the planet.

“Mum and dad, what a moment,” Kane croaked on stage. “All those years, the sacrifice, the support you gave me. Taking me to training, coming to watch me play. No matter where it was, even to this day you’re there. All those traits you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight.”
Alexia Putellas was born to reign. pic.twitter.com/NlzNmcTJei

Three years after tearing her ACL on the eve of the 2022 European Championship, shortly before claiming a second successive Ballon d’Or, Alexis Putellas had worked her way back to the podium. Barcelona’s captain during another all-conquering campaign has since taken her talents to Bromley, lighting up the WSL with London City Lionesses.

“All the boys and girls around the world,” Putellas concluded, “if you love football and if you want to play football, play football. It doesn’t matter if you’re a boy or if you’re a girl. Doesn’t matter where you come from. Don’t listen if someone tells you, you can’t do it. Believe in yourself.”

Lamine Yamal managed to fight his way past his own outfit to the award. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesLamine Yamal was crowned the Kopa Trophy winner for a third year in succession but claimed that his Barcelona teammate was more deserving of the award. “This one should have been for Pau Cubarsí.”

Vicky López is a back-to-back winner. / Jeff Spicer/UEFA/Getty Images)Much like her male counterpart at Barcelona, Yamal, Vicky López is a multi-time Kopa Trophy winner. The 2025 victor claimed the prize again after blossoming into a figure of real importance for a Barça side which reestablished their dominance on the global game.
🫂🧤 #ballondor pic.twitter.com/DdepKZoosY

Peter Schmeichel claimed that there was “no surprise” Unai Simón was recognized for his individual efforts when handing the Spanish World Cup winner the award on Monday. Yet, there had been stiff competition from his compatriots David Raya—the best goalkeeper in the Premier League—and Barcelona’s title-winning Joan García. In the end, the panel of judges sided with Luis de la Fuente, who trusted Simón above his countrymen at the World Cup.
CATA COLL IS THE 2026 WOMEN’S GOALKEEPER OF THE YEAR! #ballondor pic.twitter.com/f38udAQxM2

It was a clean sweep of Spanish goalkeeper this year, with Barcelona’s Cata Coll taking the women’s prize after presiding over a parsimonious campaign in Catalonia. Coll unfortunately had the spotlight slightly shifted away from her thanks to the hasty work of the award’s presenter, Schmeichel, who insisted upon announcing both men’s and women’s winners at the same time.

This is a purely statistical award dished out to the top scorer men’s and women’s players from the 2025–26 season for club and country. Harry Kane outstripped everyone with a staggering haul of 73 for Bayern Munich and England while Mexico’s Charlyn Corral was recognized after another prolific year at Pachuca.
We're proud of you, Bukayo ❤️ pic.twitter.com/DK7RNiAHAc

Arsenal superstar Bukayo Saka was handed the most unique prize of the night. The Sócrates award ignores all action on the pitch to instead honor the individual (or collective) to “identify the best solidarity actions carried out by committed champions.”
Saka’s work for the international charity BigShoe saw him deservedly collect an award named after the legendary Brazilian whose commitment to social causes was as legendary as his playing career.
PSG continue to show there's levels to this game. pic.twitter.com/e16uls0VM6

Paris Saint-Germain were crowned the best men’s club of the year for a second season running. Manager Luis Enrique once again snubbed the ceremony so the duty of collecting the trophy for the defending Champions League winners fell to 2026 Ballon d’Or winner, Ousmane Dembélé.
